question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 5 \\ -10 & 3\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above.
Given that $A$ has the complex eigenvalue $\lambda =-2-5\text{i},$ and that $A=PC{P}^{-1}$ where $C$ is a rotation-scaling matrix, what is the value of 
$\frac{{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}}{{c}^{2}+{d}^{2}}?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

Since we are given the eigenvalue $\lambda =-2-5\text{i},$ we can immediately construct the rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,{\lambda }_{1}=-2-5\text{i},$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & 5 \\ -10 & 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-2-5\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & -2-5\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5+5\text{i} & 5 \\ -10 & 5+5\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}(-5+5\text{i}){x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=0 \\ -10{x}_{1}+(5+5\text{i}){x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the matrix $A-\lambda I$ is singular, the system above must have a non-zero solution. This means that one equation of the system is a multiple of another. As a result, we can drop one of the rows and take one of the variables as the free variable. For example, from the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}(1+\text{i}){x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}(1+\text{i}){x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in C.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=2$, we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we can construct the matrix $P$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\frac{{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}}{{c}^{2}+{d}^{2}}=\frac{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$
